_comment: Interview knowledge the DV-100 field_config cannot express. DV-100 is the primary form of the packet, so the nameIds chosen here are canonical - DV-109 and DV-110 mirror them for the values shared across the packet (case number, party names, court address, hearing date/time). Nineteen conditionals named gates with no matching field; the eleven with a real counterpart are retargeted below, and the remaining eight are genuine gates the form implies but never stores.

additional_pages_count._why: DV-100 item 32 asks for the number of extra pages attached. A filer cannot count them and the debug fill answered 100. The packet knows: the pages of every attachment being filed, plus one for each separate sheet already promised.
additional_pages_count._whyAttachedTo: Counted along what each form says it is attached to, not along what switches it on. DV-108 is attached to DV-105, which is attached to DV-100, so its pages are part of the stack handed in with this form; DV-140 is attached to DV-110, a separate order, so its pages are not - and counting every conditional form as an attachment had put DV-140 in, making this 18 where it is 12.

other_abuse_incident_details._why: DV-100 item 7 ends with "Check this box if you need more space to describe the abuse. You can use form DV-101" - which asks a filer to predict, before writing a word, whether what they are about to say fits in a box whose size they cannot see. They need more space exactly when they have used more than the box holds, and the box has been measured.
other_abuse_incident_details._whyBeyond: DV-101 item 5 carries the same escape - "Check here if you need more space. Attach a sheet of paper" - and asking it was the same mistake one form further on. Past what both boxes hold there is a third thing that is true and knowable: the filer has more to say than the packet can print, and a sheet of their own is the only place left for it.
